newsitem.title: JAPAN: E.ASIA OILSEEDS - JAPAN QUIET, TAIWAN TO BUY BEANS.
newsitem.headline: E.ASIA OILSEEDS - JAPAN QUIET, TAIWAN TO BUY BEANS.

text.p: Japanese soybean importers are likely to stay on the sidelines this week while a Taiwanese outfit may tender for 10,000 tonnes of beans in an otherwise quiet Asian oilseeds market, regional dealers said on Monday.
The Japanese, who recently bought some U.S. crop for early-October shipments, would probably remain quiet this week due to the "obon" holidays, traders said.
"Local buyers are sidelined now, and will remain quiet until early next week," a trade house official in Japan said.
The importers are waiting for better prices and timing to get coverage of new crop U.S. soybean, the traders said.
The Taiwan Sugar Corp was scheduled to tender on Wednesday for 10,000 tonnes of soybean and 20,000 tonnes of U.S. corn for late September to early October delivery, dealers said.
But most Taiwanese soybean buyers this week would show little interest in the market this week since most of them have bought their September and October supplies, traders said.
